data.title: Ivermectin 1% cream (and 0.5% lotion)
data.body:
_Topicals · III Antiparasitics_

**Class:** Macrocyclic lactone (avermectin) — topical

## Mechanism of action
- Binds glutamate-gated chloride channels in invertebrates → paralysis of Demodex mites and lice
- Anti-inflammatory effects (reduces neutrophil activity and cytokines)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- 1% cream: papulopustular rosacea (more effective than metronidazole gel), demodicosis
- 0.5% lotion: head lice (age 6 months and older) — single 10-min application, no nit combing needed
- Scabies (off-label, compounded 1% lotion/cream)

## Dose & formulations
- Rosacea: 1% cream once daily for up to 16 weeks, then maintenance
- Head lice: 0.5% lotion to dry hair and scalp, leave 10 min, rinse — single use

## Adverse effects
- Burning, irritation, dry skin; transient rosacea flare at start

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity

## Pregnancy & lactation
Minimal absorption; limited data — avoid unless needed.

## Viva points
- Targets Demodex in rosacea
- Single-application head lice treatment

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.44; Khopkar ch.21. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
